title: Regex Groups, Named Groups and Alternation
learningObjectives: Explain capturing groups, non-capturing groups, named groups and | alternation and where they are useful.
Select the correct regex syntax or re function for capturing groups, non-capturing groups, named groups and | alternation.
Predict the output of representative PY19.4 expressions.
Identify matching, validation and performance risks related to capturing groups, non-capturing groups, named groups and | alternation.
Apply capturing groups, non-capturing groups, named groups and | alternation in a small, deterministic Python program.

understand.concept: Parentheses group parts of a pattern and can capture matched text for later use. Named groups give captures descriptive identifiers. Alternation uses the vertical bar to select one of several alternatives, and grouping controls the scope of that choice.
understand.whyItMatters: Groups make complex patterns easier to read and let programs extract meaningful fields such as a year, month or identifier prefix.
understand.analogy: Groups are labelled compartments in a matched record; alternation is a choice between allowed forms.
understand.analogyLimit: Capturing groups change the shape of findall results, and alternation order can affect which alternative is selected first.
understand.summary: Regex Groups, Named Groups and Alternation teaches readable and predictable pattern matching with Python's re module.

explain.narrative:
## Capture and organize matches
Parentheses create capturing groups. Match objects expose captures through `.group(1)`, `.groups()` and `.groupdict()`. A named group uses `(?P<name>...)` and can be retrieved by its name. A non-capturing group `(?:...)` groups alternatives without adding a capture.

The `|` operator means OR. Use parentheses to make its scope explicit, for example `(?:cat|dog)s?`. Prefer clear, bounded patterns over deeply nested expressions.

examples.title: Capture two parts of a code
examples.code:
import re
match = re.fullmatch(r'([A-Z]{2})-(\d{3})', 'AB-204')
print(match.group(1))
print(match.group(2))
examples.explanation: The first and second capturing groups return the prefix and numeric portion.

examples.title: Use a named group
examples.explanation: Named groups make extracted fields easier to understand.

examples.title: Choose between alternatives
examples.code:
import re
pattern = r'cat|dog'
print(re.findall(pattern, 'cat dog bird'))
examples.explanation: The vertical bar matches either alternative.

examples.title: Group alternatives with a shared suffix
examples.code:
import re
pattern = r'(?:cat|dog)s?'
print(re.findall(pattern, 'cat cats dog dogs'))
examples.explanation: The group selects cat or dog and the optional s applies to either choice.

examples.title: Use a non-capturing group
examples.explanation: The non-capturing group organizes alternatives without changing the returned full matches.
